facts.claim: Reported history: Brothers Dane and Travis Boersma founded Dutch Bros in Grants Pass, Oregon, in 1992. The brand grew from an espresso pushcart around beverages and personal service; drive-through convenience is central to its operating identity.

Reported financials: Q2 2026 total revenue was $550.9 million, up 32.5% from $415.8 million. Company-operated same-shop sales grew 8.3%, including 3.4% transaction growth. Company revenue and company-operated comparable sales are distinct measures.

Reported expansion: Dutch Bros opened 48 shops in Q2 2026, 44 company-operated. Inference: managers must preserve existing-shop execution while allocating staff and attention to growth. This does not establish spare local capacity.

Reported capability: Dutch Bros offers app-based Order Ahead at participating shops. Pickup availability varies by location. This does not establish that every location in a hypothetical pilot market supports the feature.

Assumed local remit: The player controls 12 participating company-operated shops near some of the Starbucks pilot cafés. It can adjust shifts, app messaging and local acquisition offers, but cannot open a new shop within the three-round horizon.
sources: Author-designed simulation assumption, 2026-09-12; not a company disclosure or measured customer observation.

facts.claim: Assumed commercial envelope: Maximum incremental acquisition and labor budget $30,000 across these 12 shops per month. A $1 trial credit is a permitted option, not a precommitted action. Local variable contribution, queue capacity and cohort acquisition cost are unknown and must be estimated or measured before scaling.
